title: Handover Grace Carried on a Keyturn Guest Protection Plan Election
content:
Cover under the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan begins when the vehicle changes hands rather than at the
reserved hour, and a handover grace is added to the election for the day the vehicle changes hands. How much
grace is added follows where the vehicle is handed over, as the delivery recorded on the Keyturn Trip Booking
shows it.

| Where the vehicle is handed over | Handover grace added |
|---|---|
| Delivered to the guest at an airport | 2 days |
| Delivered to the guest anywhere else | 1 day |
| Collected by the guest themselves | 0 days |

**The rule in one sentence.** Where the vehicle is delivered to the guest at an airport, 2 days of handover
grace are added; where the vehicle is delivered to the guest anywhere else, 1 day is added; where the guest
collects the vehicle themselves, none is added.

## Points of judgement

**An airport delivery and a kerbside delivery are not the same case.** Both are deliveries to the guest, but
only a delivery at an airport carries the 2 days; a delivery to a home address, an office or a hotel is a
delivery anywhere else and carries 1 day.

**A collection is not a delivery.** Where the guest goes to the vehicle and takes it themselves, nothing is
delivered, and the grace added is 0 days.

**Hypothetical readings.** A trip whose vehicle is delivered to an airport terminal adds 2 days of handover
grace to the election. The same trip, with the vehicle delivered instead to the guest's home, adds 1. The same
trip again, with the guest walking to where the car is parked and taking it, adds nothing at all.
